title: Rugged tablet for IFS Ultimo (Ultimo Go+ app)
meta_description: Rugged Android tablets for the Ultimo Go+ app (Android 8.0 and up, offline, camera scanning). Tuga A10 and A6 run Android 14 and 15. UK business seller.
intro: IFS Ultimo is a cloud-based Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) and CMMS platform used by maintenance, facilities, fleet and HSE teams in manufacturing, food and beverage, chemicals, healthcare, logistics and utilities. The vendor has a UK office in Staines and publishes UK customer cases including London Gatwick Airport, Victrex, National Grid Nemo Link, the Manufacturing Technology Centre and Bristol Port Company. The field app is Ultimo Go+, published by IFS Ultimo B.V. for Android and iOS.

On the floor or on site, technicians use Ultimo Go+ to process activities and inspections, report new activities, look up equipment, inventory, buildings, suppliers and contracts, attach photos from the camera, use GPS, and scan QR codes and barcodes. The vendor states the app keeps working when the device is temporarily disconnected. That means the device is in use in plant rooms, on gantries, in vehicles and outdoors, where a tablet without an ingress rating or a drop rating is at more risk of damage than it would be at a desk.

This page sets out what the vendor publishes about device requirements for Ultimo Go+, which Tuga device fits those requirements, where the Windows option does and does not apply, and how UK business buyers can trial one unit before ordering a fleet.

requirements.requirement: Android 8.0 and up for the Ultimo Go+ app
requirements.detail: The Google Play listing for Ultimo Go+ (package com.ultimo.UltimoGoPlus, developer IFS Ultimo B.V.) requires Android 8.0 and up. The Tuga A10 runs Android 14 and the Tuga A6 runs Android 15, which both meet this requirement.

The Play and App Store listings state: "Even if you are temporarily disconnected, you can continue working." and list "Available offline: working without an internet connection" as a feature. The vendor's Ultimo Mobile page states that offline working requires Ultimo Go+ rather than the online-only Ultimo Go. The vendor does not publish how much data is cached or how sync conflicts are handled.

requirements.requirement: Camera for QR and barcode scanning and for photos
requirements.detail: The app lists "Scanning (QR code, barcode)" and "Camera integration (linking photos)" as features. No dedicated scan engine or scanner SDK requirement is published, so scanning is done through the device camera.
The Play listing lists "GPS integration" as a feature of Ultimo Go+, so a device with a GPS receiver is needed to use it.

requirements.requirement: Windows: desktop web client only, no Windows build of Ultimo Go+
requirements.detail: The vendor's Ultimo Mobile page states that Ultimo Go+ is available "via the Apple Store (iOS) or the Google Play Store (Android)". No Windows app or Microsoft Store listing was found. The vendor's CMMS page describes the system as a cloud-based solution running on Microsoft Azure, accessed from desktop and mobile devices, and does not publish a supported-browser list or PC requirements.

requirements.requirement: NFC and RFID: not listed as Ultimo Go+ features
requirements.detail: The current Google Play and App Store descriptions, the App Store release history and the public ultimo.com pages we checked do not list NFC or RFID tag reading among Ultimo Go+ features. We do not claim it works. If tag reading matters to you, confirm it with IFS Ultimo before buying. The NFC on Tuga devices is a hardware fact only.

requirements.requirement: No published hardware or screen-size guidance
requirements.detail: IFS Ultimo publishes no recommended devices, hardware requirements or screen-size guidance on its public pages; its Ultimo Mobile page says "Contact us for the required hardware and software" and describes using the app "on your tablet or smartphone". The only published requirements are the store minimums (Android 8.0 and up; iOS/iPadOS 15.0 or later). The cloud page states only that the mobile app "runs with the minimum privileges required on the operating system."

recommended.why: Ultimo Go+ is an Android app with a published minimum of Android 8.0 and up, and the Tuga A10 runs Android 14, so it meets that requirement. The A10 gives technicians a 10.1 inch FHD screen for work orders, inspection checklists and equipment records, a 13MP rear camera with flash for the app's camera-based QR and barcode scanning and photo linking, GPS for the app's GPS integration, and 4G dual SIM for connectivity between sites, with the app's own offline mode covering gaps in coverage. IP68 and MIL-STD-810H ratings and an operating range of -20 to 60C suit plant rooms, yards and outdoor assets. An industrial asset-management firm has already bought a Tuga A10 for maintenance technicians running a different mobile maintenance app at an aerospace manufacturer.
fit: Android 8.0 and up required: the A10 runs Android 14.

Camera-based QR and barcode scanning and photo linking: 13MP rear camera with flash, 5MP front camera. There is no dedicated scan engine, so scanning depends on the app's camera support, which the vendor lists.
GPS integration: GPS + Galileo + BeiDou receiver.
Offline working and site-to-site travel: 4G dual SIM, dual-band Wi-Fi 5, 8000mAh battery, 128GB storage with microSD up to 2TB.
Shift-long use in industrial environments: IP68, MIL-STD-810H, tempered glass, -20 to 60C operating temperature, 680g, hand strap in the box.

recommended.why: The Tuga A8 runs Android 12 and therefore meets the Android 8.0 and up requirement for Ultimo Go+. At 8 inches it is the middle size, with more room for work orders and inspection checklists than the A6 in a smaller body than the A10, and its 1000 nit screen helps when reading jobs on outdoor assets or in sunlit yards. Its 8000mAh battery is removable, so a charged spare can take over on a long shift, and VESA mount points with a pogo pin connector let it dock in a vehicle between sites. It costs £379, £70 less than the A10, but it is IP67 rather than IP68, has no MIL-STD rating, runs Android 12 rather than Android 14, has a lower 1280 x 800 resolution and has 6GB RAM against the A10's 8GB; IFS Ultimo publishes no RAM figure to check against.
fit: Android 8.0 and up required: the A8 runs Android 12 with Google Play.

Camera-based QR and barcode scanning and photo linking: 13MP autofocus rear camera with flash, 5MP front camera. There is no dedicated scan engine, so scanning depends on the app's camera support, which the vendor lists.
GPS integration: GPS + GLONASS + Galileo + BeiDou receiver.
Offline working and site-to-site travel: 4G LTE dual SIM, Wi-Fi, removable 8000mAh battery, 128GB storage with a microSD slot.
Outdoor and vehicle use: 8 inch IPS 1280 x 800 screen at 1000 nits under AGC glass, IP67, VESA mount points and a pogo pin connector.

recommended.why: The Tuga A6 runs Android 15 and therefore meets the Android 8.0 and up requirement for Ultimo Go+. It is the choice where technicians want a pocketable handheld rather than a tablet, at 277g, and where a lot of asset labels are scanned: it has a Zebra 2D scan engine with two side scan keys as well as a 13MP rear camera with flash. The vendor documents camera scanning, so test whether Ultimo Go+ accepts input from the scan engine before relying on it. The 6 inch screen is smaller than the A10's 10.1 inch display, so long inspection forms and asset hierarchies involve more scrolling, and it has 4GB RAM and 64GB storage against the A10's 8GB and 128GB. IP67, a 1.5 metre drop rating and a removable 5050mAh battery suit long shifts, though IP67 is not a wash-down rating.
fit: Android 8.0 and up required: the A6 runs Android 15.
QR and barcode scanning and photo linking: 13MP rear camera with flash, plus a Zebra 2D scan engine (support for scan engine input is not documented by the vendor).
GPS integration: GPS + GLONASS + BeiDou + Galileo receiver.
Offline working and reconnection: 4G LTE dual SIM, dual-band Wi-Fi 5, removable 5050mAh battery, 64GB storage with microSD up to 256GB.
Handheld use on site: 277g, IP67, 1.5 metre drop rating, -20 to 50C.

recommended.why: The Tuga W10 does not run Ultimo Go+, because the vendor publishes the app for Android and iOS only. It is an option only for the browser-based desktop client, which the vendor says is accessed from desktop devices, for example a planner or supervisor at a workshop bench or in a van who needs the full desktop view, a wired Ethernet connection or an HDMI output to a larger screen. The vendor publishes no supported-browser list, so we can only say that the W10 runs Windows 11 Pro with a full desktop browser. Its IP65 rating protects against dust and water jets but not immersion.
fit: Browser-based desktop client: Windows 11 Pro with a full desktop browser on a 10.1 inch 1280 x 800 multi-touch display.
Fixed or workshop use: 100Mbps RJ45 Ethernet, HDMI, USB-A, USB-C, pogo pin dock connector.
Mobile use between locations: optional 4G LTE and GPS, dual-band Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 5.2, removable 5000mAh battery (run time depends on load).
Dust and spray in workshops: IP65 (dust tight, protected against water jets, not rated for immersion).

setup_steps: Confirm with your IFS Ultimo administrator that your edition and user licences cover the technicians who will use Ultimo Go+, and that mobile access is enabled for their accounts.

On the Tuga A10, A8 or A6, sign in to a Google account, open Google Play, search for Ultimo Go+ (publisher IFS Ultimo B.V.) and install it. Android 14 on the A10, Android 12 on the A8 and Android 15 on the A6 all meet the app's Android 8.0 and up requirement.
Open the app and sign in with the credentials and environment details your administrator provides.

Before the first shift, open the app on Wi-Fi and let it download its data, then test it with Wi-Fi and mobile data switched off to confirm the offline working described by the vendor behaves as you expect for your data volume.
Grant camera and location permissions when the app asks, then test a QR or barcode scan on an existing asset label and a photo attachment on a test activity.
Fit the hand strap (A10, in the box) or tempered glass screen protector, and add a vehicle mounting dock or charging dock where the device will live between jobs.
accessories: Charging dock, £49.99 (A10, W10), so devices return to a known place at shift end and start charged
Vehicle mounting dock, £109, for engineers who travel between sites in a van
Tempered glass screen protector 2-pack, £14, for screens that get scanned against dirty labels all day
Belt holster, £22 (A6), to keep the handheld to hand and both hands free on ladders and gantries

faq.q: Will Ultimo Go+ run on the Tuga A10 and A6?
faq.a: The Google Play listing for Ultimo Go+ requires Android 8.0 and up. The Tuga A10 runs Android 14 and the Tuga A6 runs Android 15, which both meet that requirement. IFS Ultimo does not publish a list of recommended or supported devices, so we state the published requirement and the device's operating system, nothing more. We welcome a single trial unit so you can confirm the app on your own Ultimo environment before ordering more.

faq.q: Does Ultimo Go+ work offline on a rugged tablet?
faq.a: Yes, according to the vendor. The Play and App Store listings state that if you are temporarily disconnected you can continue working, and list working without an internet connection as a feature. The vendor does not publish how much data is cached or how conflicts are resolved on sync, so test this with your own data before rollout. The A10 and A6 both have 4G dual SIM for reconnecting between sites.

faq.q: Can we run IFS Ultimo on the Tuga W10 Windows tablet?
faq.a: Only the browser-based desktop client. The vendor publishes Ultimo Go+ for Android and iOS, and no Windows version or Microsoft Store listing was found. The W10 runs Windows 11 Pro with a full desktop browser, has Ethernet and HDMI, and is IP65 rated (not for immersion). IFS Ultimo does not publish a supported-browser list, so check with your administrator.

faq.q: Can we trial one unit, and do you invoice businesses?
faq.a: Yes to both. Business buyers can request a quote and pay by bank transfer on a proforma invoice, and a single trial unit before a fleet order is welcome. Tuga Hardware is not VAT registered, so there is no VAT to add to the listed prices. Multi-unit discounts apply automatically: 3% at 2 units, 5% at 3 to 4, 8% at 5 to 9 and 10% at 10 or more. Delivery is free worldwide in 7 to 10 working days, with 30-day returns and a 12-month warranty.

faq.q: Should we choose the 10.1 inch A10 or the 6 inch A6?
faq.a: IFS Ultimo publishes no screen-size guidance, so this is a workflow choice. The A10's 10.1 inch 1920 x 1200 screen suits long inspection forms, asset hierarchies and photo review, and it is the primary pick at £449. The A6 at £349 is a 277g handheld with a 6 inch FHD+ screen, a Zebra 2D scan engine, a removable 5050mAh battery and IP67, which suits technicians who need a pocketable device or scan a lot of labels, though it has 4GB RAM against the A10's 8GB. The A10 runs Android 14 and the A6 Android 15, and both have NFC as a hardware feature, though the current Ultimo Go+ store descriptions do not list NFC or RFID among the app's features.

not_recommended_note: The vendor publishes Ultimo Go+ for Android and iOS only, so the Tuga W10 cannot run the field app; it is suitable only for the browser-based desktop client, and IFS Ultimo publishes no supported-browser list or PC requirements. The W10's optional 2D barcode scanner and optional UHF RFID reader do not help with Ultimo Go+ because the app does not run on Windows. The current store descriptions and the public vendor pages we checked do not list NFC or RFID among Ultimo Go+ features, so do not buy on the basis of tag reading without confirming it with IFS Ultimo; the NFC in the A10, A8 and A6 is a hardware feature only. Scanning in Ultimo Go+ is through the camera. The A10 and A6 both have rear cameras. The A10 has no dedicated scan engine, and the A6's Zebra 2D scan engine is not documented by the vendor as supported, so scanning depends on the app's camera support. The vendor publishes no recommended devices, so none of the devices on this page is tested, approved or certified by IFS Ultimo.
